title: After Playing Infinity Nikki 3.0 for Four Hours, its New Cities and Outfits Are Just Some of the Additions Worth Returning For
summary: The new 3.0 update has tons of new stuff to explore including new locations, outfits and gameplay systems, although don't expect any kind of proper challenge.
content: When Infinity Nikki first launched in 2024, it introduced players around the world to the dress-up world of mobile game star Nikki in her first 3D console/PC adventure, an open world filled with wholesome fun, fashion and friendship. 2025’s V2.0 update introduced a new area to the world of Miraland, as well as new ways to traverse it. But now with the new V3.0 update titled Of Yesterday and Tomorrow, Nikki’s wonderful world has been expanded significantly – with its richest locations yet, and even a cute convertible to traverse it with. To give you an idea of how huge this update is, I played for over four hours at developer Infold’s Shanghai office, focusing mainly on story content and with only the slightest bit of open-world exploration and lifestyle simulation gameplay, and didn't even see all of one of its two new cities. The golden path apparently offers some nine hours of story content, with two dense and exciting new areas to get lost in. Between the V3.0 launch and Nikki’s birthday celebration campaign, players can get 160 free draws and 19 new sets of clothing. I spent most of my time in Cicia, a city of art, based loosely on Paris among other places, and lined with cobblestone streets and beatific brickwork architecture. Cicia was previously featured as a location in the mobile game Shining Nikki, and makes its 3D debut here. It’s a world where art nouveau, belle epoque and art deco collide, and home to the Cicia Art Academy where Miraland’s most promising students are taught lessons of art creation and appraisal by the finest tutors. When Nikki receives an invitation to study there, she and her catlike companion Momo embark on a new adventure of aesthetic discovery. But is everything at the academy truly as it seems? Some of the outfits in the update grant Nikki new skills. Unlock and craft the preppy four-star Leaping Breeze outfit to gain a higher double-jump and airborne dash abilities, while the much darker and sexier Night’s Hidden Side outfit allows Nikki to “bind” with objects around the environment (think Mario’s possession skill in Mario Odyssey) and use them to warp to hard-to-reach places. These new skills allow for a new level of verticality in Cicia’s map and dungeons, helping you explore the castle spires or negotiate intricate dungeon maps. You can also find a musket for long-range attacks (which is a new Whimtech item), and dress for the occasion in Cicia’s three-star, nine-piece outfit Song of Endless Youth. V3.0 also introduces a new outfit category, Star Crown Resonance. The Star Crown Resonance outfit named Where Stars Shine Again comes with a musket and staff, and is designed for tougher combat situations. With either weapon equipped, Nikki’s unused dashes are stored, and you can release them all at once or use them one at a time, creating a sort of combo system that deals more damage. While previous Infinity Nikki maps tended towards countryside locations, Cicia is a bustling city. Arriving by airship to take in the stunning views, Nikki and Momo step into a throng of students, teachers and residents, each with voiced dialogue to idly eavesdrop on as they prepare for a huge school festival, building an air of excitement as Nikki starts academy life. In this maelstrom of culture, recruiters for the drama club and literature club compete for Nikki’s attention. And then she meets Béatrice Laviolette. A young ducal heiress, at first Béatrice is quite brusque, standoffish and snobby. It started to feel like meeting Glinda in the heightened magical environs of Shiz University, and when it was announced in a cutscene that the students would compete for the right to wear a legendary Miracle Outfit, I assumed Nikki and Béatrice were heading into a bitter rivalry. But Nikki has always been a relentlessly positive character, with a deep and forgiving heart and a desire to encourage those around her. Without wanting to spoil anything, let’s just say that she, Béatrice and earnest classmate Déphine Garnier foster a relationship that may surprise you. Meanwhile, fellow student Sikong Ran invites Nikki to join his Society of Whispers and Wonders, a supernatural-obsessed group who study things that go boo in the night – lending more than a little taste of Wednesday or Riverdale high-school mystery. Exploring the city is a reward unto itself. Rich and bustling with life, it features picturesque sunsets, glittering lakes, colourful flowerbeds, gargling fountains. It is filled with side missions and simple minigames, including one where you construct a street band to perform jolly jazz music in the castle plaza. In the streets, teachers guide students through artistic concepts that are interesting to read – for example, did you know that in music, technical perfection is no match for the heart of the musician? The characters you meet are endearing; and as before, the dialogue is filled with gentle humour – not least the central relationship between Nikki and Momo, which remains as heartwarming as ever. But as you progress, Nikki learns that behind the magic of this idyllic city, there is a dark secret. Using her new binding skill to unravel environmental puzzles, she is drawn into a conspiracy that only Nikki can solve. As part of this, I got to play through one of two new dungeons, titled The Ideal City. This is a clockwork house of tricks that recalls the steampunk-coded vibe of earlier Infinity Nikki dungeons, with huge cogs that alter the mechanical environments as they turn, and wooden theatre dioramas folding in and out of view in the background as you progress. Half of the exploration takes the form of platforming action, which, like previous Infinity Nikki dungeons, is not exactly a tough challenge, but enough to make use of Nikki’s new jump and dash abilities and test your reactions a little. The other half is made up of environmental puzzles that use Nikki’s new bind ability, tasking you with scanning the area of objects to possess and manipulate in order to progress – for example, turning keys or bouncing between bird-shaped statues on high-up ledges. In one section, you even possess a giant glass marble and manoeuvre it along tight, narrow ledges, like Super Monkey Ball. The variety of gameplay on offer is strong, and, combined with the fantastic art design and hummable jazzy soundtrack, makes up for the lack of a tougher challenge. Speaking of which, I also got to try a boss battle from later in the campaign, making use of Nikki’s battle-ready Where Stars Shine Again outfit for more powerful combos. I was able to beat the boss on my first try. But Infinity Nikki isn’t really supposed to be a hardcore action experience, and the drama of the scene and the story beats that lead up to it should satisfy fans, while offering some mild challenge to younger players. Also in Cicia, I got to try the new driving system. Up until now, Nikki has largely travelled on foot or by bicycle, but now she has a range of vehicles to choose from – and fun ways to use them. You can get your own convertible, pay in-game currency to rent a classic car, and unlock even more. While driving, you can change the radio stations like in GTA, engage in Uber-style mini-missions like in Crazy Taxi, or simply drive to your destination. The car even has a jump button. But what impressed me the most is how photo mode has been integrated here. Infinity Nikki has had a strong photo mode since launch, allowing players to dress and pose Nikki and Momo to their satisfaction and snap them at will. I wondered if it would work while she was in the driver’s seat – and I was pleasantly surprised to find that not only does it work, it comes with a wealth of car-specific customisation options – such as opening or closing the doors, switching the head lamps on or off, and raising or lowering the convertible roof. These thoughtful touches enhanced my time spent with Nikki on the road, and show just how much care and attention have gone into this new update. Did I mention that Cicia is only one of two new areas? I spent just a little bit of time in Ceremius, a city with more of a dark fantasy style. Here a terrible earthquake has upended the city, while some magical force has held it together in surreal ways. But while the post-disaster atmosphere is undoubtedly more sombre and intense than in Cicia, the city is still densely populated with residents. The art theme also remains, with a plethora of statues and installations to find. Clicking on one bizarre statue, I got a paragraph of smartly written critique, explaining the work with the eye of an art collector. Ceremius also features a new set of alchemy abilities, which I didn't have time to try, but promise to add even more depth to an already packed content update. During my time with Of Yesterday and Tomorrow, it was a pleasure to return to Nikki’s fashion-friendly world. In particular, Cicia and Ceremius are introduced in impressive detail, and I felt like I was not only exploring a real place, but enjoying the design team’s eye for art as well, as the story presents artworks, fashion and musical theatre in a way that actually lets you experience them directly. The update drops today, so jump in and dress up to see for yourself. Daniel Robson is the Executive Producer of IGN Japan.

title: Amazon Has the Best Family Board Game Deals Under $15 for Black Friday
content: Tabletop gaming can be an expensive hobby if you're not careful. Some of the best modern board games can get pretty expensive, even with a Black Friday discount attached. If you're just looking to add some fun family games to your collection, however, it can be really quite affordable. Amazon has a number of Lightning Deals going on right now that drop prices well under $15 for some great games. Note : All of these discounts are Amazon Lightning Deals , which means there's a limit to how many people can get the deal. Once a deal is fully claimed, the discounted price will likely disappear. There's a nice mix of old and new board games getting discounts here. You've got classics like Clue, Candy Land, Connect 4, and Chutes and Ladders as well as some wild cards like Pigs on Trampolines and Taco Cat Goat Cheese Pizza. These are all games that the whole family can play, though many of them do lean more toward younger kids . More Family Board Game Deal Recommendations If you're willing to spend a little more, there are also some great family board games for under $25 right now as well. One of IGN's top picks for the category is Harmonies, which is a delightful habitat building game up to four players can play. We gave it an 8 out of 10 in our review , calling it a "satisfying blend of drafting and spatial puzzle-solving wrapped in a beautifully designed package." For those more interested in trick-taking games, there's also a great deal on The Fellowship of the Ring version of the genre. We gave it an 8 out of 10 in our review , saying: Its simple rules and working together gameplay make it great for families, but its twists on the trick-taking formula and storytelling beats make it deserve a much wider audience."

title: Chainsaws 'Would Have Been Too Much' Even for GTA 6, as Rockstar Explains Why Some Extra Violent Weapons Are Missing
summary: Rockstar has explained why some extra violent weapons like chainsaws and katanas are missing from GTA 6.
content: You can commit an extreme amount of violence in GTA 6 , with a wide variety of weaponry. Guns, baseball bats, even tanks can be your chosen tool of destruction. But that hasn’t stopped some from wondering where some series favourites have disappeared to. Among those are the likes of katanas and chainsaws, which were staples during Grand Theft Auto’s “3D universe” games, including Vice City and San Andreas. The chainsaw, in particular, holds a special connection to Vice City given its clear Scarface inspirations, and memorable scene involving the power tool from the 1983 movie. But despite some being spotted around the latest version of Leonida in GTA 6, neither Jason nor Lucia can wield them as weapons. Why? Well, Rockstar co-studio head Rob Nelson explained the decision in an interview with VGC . “As far as the chainsaw — I think it would have been too much for this game at this resolution and these characters,” Nelson says. "It’s not a resource thing. Even at the most psycho, did Jason and Lucia really need that — what’s that going to look like?” When asked specifically about why chainsaws are lying about the world, but can’t be picked up, Nelson explained that, “you’re always trying to find what is the right sort of line and the right balance; it really just depends — you want to feel like you can interact with as much of the world as possible.” I have to somewhat agree that it just wouldn’t feel like it fit either Jason or Lucia’s characters to be roaming around looking for limbs to chop off with a mechanised serrated blade. Ultimately, their story is one about committing crime to escape to a better, more “normal” life, not one about two psychopaths with a lust for blood going on a rampage. That being said, when whatever the online component of GTA 6 launches, I could see objects like this becoming weapons, allowing for people to roleplay as whatever brand of criminal, psychopath, or tree sculptor they wish. title: Creating Fresh Looks Is More Important in GTA 6 Than Any Game Before
summary: GTA 6 has Rockstar's best-ever customisation, with hundreds of amazing pieces. But it's about more that creating a fresh fit - clothes are key to surviving the cops.
content: This is an opinion piece from writer Jess Kinghorn. IGN's opinion columns represent the personal viewpoints of the writer, drawing on their own experiences and research to explore the exciting world of video games. There comes a time in every professional criminal’s life when you’ve got to make a dear friend disappear. I’ll keep the spoilers light on when that happens in Grand Theft Auto 6 , but all you need to know is that our man Jason has been tasked with getting rid of a former contact’s car – plus all of their worldly possessions. Now, had I actually checked the trunk I would have seen a bright red gas can and then set the whole thing ablaze – unfortunately, I didn’t check the trunk. Instead, I drove the departed’s wheels straight into Leonida Bay in full view of witnesses. Now, our lad Jason is a wanted man looking to disappear himself. Camped out in a bush, the police scanner crackles to life. “Suspect is a white male wearing a baseball cap” – well, the cap's the first thing to go, then, as I leg it back to the Ganado. I could keep running and try to outpace the police’s BOLO, but GTA 6 offers a fair few options for escaping suspicion. Losing yourself in customisation and creating a well-stocked wardrobe has become well worth your while beyond simply looking sharp, and it’s now as much a part of your criminal arsenal as carrying a piece. I didn’t fully appreciate how GTA 6’s wealth of customisation options and the Wanted system interact until chapter two. I was already looking forward to playing dress up with Lucia, so when my new drug-shifting mum-doing-her-best pal Vicki points out the local vintage store, I can’t help but rub my grubby little gamer mitts together. But besides introducing more fashion options I’m personally inclined towards, chapter two also introduces new crimes to commit. Stick-ups are hit-it-and-quit-it criminal operations – brandish a gun, take the money, and then run. Lucia got her criminal start boosting cars when she was a young teen, so carjacking is a big, lucrative part of this chapter as well. These opportunistic crimes are a complementary contrast to chapter one’s more organised approach – but better yet, Lucia's working for herself rather than Jason playing passive errand boy. Dispatch advises to be on the lookout for someone matching my description. It's all the excuse I need to finally check out the vintage store. But, my Lucia has too much business to take care of to waste time hiding in bushes, waiting for the heat to subside. Sure, in a stick-up, I can scout around for security camera footage and destroy it like a true professional, or try to control a crowd to stop someone calling the police. Still though, it's tough to be a solo act when Lucia is striking out on her own – given my twitchy trigger fingers have flubbed entering the safe code three times already, I can't rely on making a clean exit every time. As Lucia pelts out the back door, I keep an ear out for the police scanner on her phone (I’m not gonna think too hard about how that would actually work in real life, and I'm definitely not gonna Google it). Right on cue dispatch says “Suspect is a slim woman in her twenties” (Dispatch, you flatter me), and advises nearby personnel to be on the lookout for someone matching that description, wearing a bandana, a leather jacket, and cargo pants. Well, that’s all the excuse I need to finally check out the vintage store Vicki recommended earlier. Stashing the bandana and putting on a more friendly face, I use my very recently ill-gotten gains to buy a whole new look. All the usual frumpy suspects are here – well worn trainers, faded sweatshirts, holy-moly jeans – but there are plenty of bangers too. When I’m done, Lucia strides out of the vintage store a whole new woman in a red dress and a pair of trainers a sneaker head would approve of. But diving into a clothes store and improvising a fresh outfit is just one avenue for misdirection. After a fair few stick-ups, I’ve amassed quite a collection of second hand clothes. Hats, sunglasses, and – like in Red Dead Redemption 2 – bandanas (plus plenty of other 'masks') can be used to hide your face in a pinch. Checking in with the wardrobe at Lucia’s home base, I’ve lost a lot of time composing great fits and saving them for later. It’s a particularly worthwhile time sink as you can then stow these saved outfits in the trunk of your go-to getaway vehicle (for me, that’s an Imponte Ruiner '82 in bright red). Suspect is a woman wearing a baseball cap and a yellow shirt? Not anymore, she’s not. That’s the secret of any great improviser – they’re not so much making it up as they go along, as they are phenomenally well prepared for every eventuality. And with the way playing dress up in GTA 6 now interacts with the Wanted system, I can play a whole load of different roles. You can tell a lot about a community based on what turns up in their secondhand shops, and Port Gellhorn’s selection communicates the dire financial straits many of the locals are in. Customisation doesn’t begin and end with bits of tat you find at Leonida’s second hand shops either. The Wanted system can also keep tabs on how Lucia and Jason’s hair is styled, so popping into the salon frequently is another great shout. There, you can change the style of your protagonist’s hair, the length, and the colour, too – though I do kind of wish I could sling a wig or two in the trunk of my getaway car just to cover all of my bases (especially considering the platinum blonde number Lucia wears in at least one story mission). Still, when she rocks up with freshly braided hair, Jason says he likes the new look – and that’s really what it’s all about. While Lucia is at it in the salon, she can also play around with make up. The full face looks are pretty limited to begin with, though these – and all other categories of customisation options – open up the more of Leonida you explore. As for Jason, well, we all know facial hair is like contour for men. Speaking of Lucia’s other half, clothes shopping can also factor into the duo’s relationship. I take the boy to that local vintage spot, Bargain World, and buy him a whole new fit to better complement his shaved-head-incognito-look. Judging by the little pink heart that pops up, Jason appreciates Lucia’s thoughtfulness – and perhaps even enjoys being spoiled from time to time. With how frequently you’re expected to be committing crimes in chapter two, you’re encouraged to change the look of both protagonists a lot . That’s just as well because every clothing shop, every mom and pop, every salon has different cosmetic options to play with. Heck, even the gun shop offers camo fits and cringe graphic tees (in particular, the image of a smoking shotgun barrel and the words ‘American aromatherapy’ above it sticks in the mind). I can’t wait to see all Vice City proper has to offer on the customisation front, which promises well-stocked malls and much more. For now though, I’m stuck in Port Gellhorn and making the most of its distinctly down to earth vibe. Don’t get me wrong, I did find some gems at that vintage shop – case in point, I found a graphic vest emblazoned with a pair of fanged, luscious lips and the words ‘Pussycat’ that I kind of wish was in my real life wardrobe. Unfortunately, the nicest thing I can say about the jewellery selection is that it’s neat you can layer multiple necklaces on top of one another for different looks. To be fair, you can tell a lot about a community based on what turns up in their secondhand shops, and Port Gellhorn’s ‘vintage’ selection goes some way to communicating the dire financial straits many of the locals are in. As such, a fistful of rings that don’t look all that dissimilar to the junk I’ve seen drop shippers flogging in real life will do for a bit of bling right now. Thankfully though, in GTA 6’s criminal sandbox, the next wardrobe refresh is never far. The Official GTA 6 Guide, Only on IGN Want to get the most out of your GTA 6 playthrough? title: Digital Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 Games Are $30 for Black Friday
content: Update Nov 26, 7pm ET: Stock is now gone for all of these games. There's a chance Walmart will get more codes once Black Friday actually rolls around. I'll update this page if so. Here's some excellent news for anyone with a Switch or Switch 2: the Nintendo Black Friday deals are incredibly strong this year. Stronger than ever, really. Nintendo is known as a company that barely ever runs discounts, and when it does, they're pretty weak compared to other game makers. This year, though, retailers like Amazon and Walmart are taking the lead and dropping prices incredibly low. To wit: four digital Switch and Switch 2 games just dropped to $30 at Walmart. We're talking Donkey Kong Bananza, Kirby Air Riders, and more. Let's take a look. The games in question are the Nintendo Switch 2 games Donkey Kong Bananza, Kirby Air Riders, Super Mario Party Jamboree + Jamboree TV, and the original Switch compilation Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2. That last one is a port of the 3D Mario classics from the Wii generation, if you can remember that far back. All of these games are well worth the $30 price tag. Donkey Kong Bananza was made by the same team behind the stunning Switch platformer Super Mario Odyssey. We gave Donkey Kong Bananza a 10/10 score in our review , with critic Logan Plant writing, "Donkey Kong Bananza is a truly groundbreaking 3D platformer, with satisfying movement, powerful abilities, impressive destructible environments, and clever challenges that all come together in complete harmony to create Nintendo’s first Switch 2 masterpiece." Kirby Air Riders, meanwhile, is an often-overlooked racer from the minds behind Super Smash Bros. Logan Plant gave it an 8/10 in our review , writing, "Kirby Air Riders' unconventional controls can get in its own way sometimes, but they don't stop it from being a fun, frantic action racing game with an almost unreal amount of stuff to do." Super Mario Party Jamboree + Jamboree TV is a souped-up port of the 2024 Switch game. In our review , (once again) Logan Plant wrote, "Super Mario Party Jamboree itself is still fantastic, but the mixed new content of the Switch 2 Edition + Jamboree TV re-release adds frustrating limitations and strange design decisions to what was otherwise a polished, customizable experience." Still, for $30, it's well worth it. And as for the Mario Galaxy collection? We didn't give it a straight-up review since mostly just direct ports of the Wii originals, but with controls that work better on Switch. It's a terrific pair of games that play great on Switch or Switch 2. It's unclear how much digital stock Walmart has for these games. And at this Black Friday price, it's likely to go fast. So grab the games you want sooner than later. title: Everything You Need To Know Ahead of The Delta Force Invitationals Grand Final
content: After last year’s inaugural event in Hangzhou, this weekend sees the Delta Force Invitational make its first move outside Asia, as an official competitive title at DreamHack in Stockholm, Sweden, from 27th-29th November. The Grand Final of the tournament will take place on November 29th at 11am UTC+0 through to 4pm UTC+0 after three days of global competitive action. It’s the first Chinese esports title to reach DreamHack, featuring teams that have been selected through a full professional league system. Six regions offered a route to the offline finals, and the twelve squads competing this weekend are as follows: Americas: Spacestation Gaming and GODL, via the 2026 RISE Series Americas Chinese Mainland: TES, RSG and IBG, via the Delta Force Pro League Korea: Nongshim RedForce, via RISE Series Korea Japan: FENNEL, via the 2026 Delta Force: Invitational Japan Qualifier Pan-Pacific: RX, MKK and ONIC via the Pan-Pacific Operations Cup S2 EMEA: Alliance and Fnatic, via the 2026 RISE Series EMEA Fnatic are, of course, well known to DreamHack audiences, having won the first League of Legends World Championship there back in 2011, as well as the first CS:GO Major in 2013. Alliance, being a Swedish team, will be playing on home soil, but only time will tell if this gives them an additional boost. They, and the ten other teams to have gone the distance, will once again be competing for a share of a $500,000 prize pool. One core aspect of Delta Force that’s attracted new fans over the last twelve months is its commitment to extraction as an esport. Whereas in traditional FPS competitions there’s an obvious focus on winning fights, in Delta Force’s Operations mode, information gathering, firefights, resource management and extraction decisions all play out within a single match. Viewers who tune in to watch on Twitch via @DeltaForceGameOfficial or @DeltaForce_Esports can also bag a bunch of in-game rewards: 15 minutes: Armament Voucher 20 minutes: Calling Card - Delta Force Invitational 30 minutes: Standing Gear Ticket 45 minutes: AKM - Wandering Dragon 60 minutes: Action - Cheer Plus, GOTAGA, HutchMF, Summit1G, Panda and Timmy will also be streaming the matches on their channels during the event. There’s also a tonne of in-game incentives around the event, so be sure to login between the 11th November and 3rd December to get your hands on these: Log in for 1 day during the event - DFI-themed Spray Paint ×1 Log in for a total of 2 days - Elite Gear Ticket ×2 Log in for a total of 3 days - Featured Keycard Copy Pack ×1 Log in for a total of 4 days - Elite Gear Ticket ×2 If you correctly predict the outcome of the Invitational in-game, there’s a couple of other other rewards to be had: One of your selected teams reaches the Grand Final - Cosmetic Item: ASV - Northern Frontier - Assault Vehicle ×1 One of your selected teams wins the championship - Cosmetic Item: Overtime - AK 12 - Unstoppable (orange-tier weapon) In the two years since its launch, Delta Force has steadily gained momentum, with developers Team Jade determined to grow the tactical FPS into a globally recognised esports title. With three days of intense competition on the horizon, its future certainly looks bright. Delta Force is free to play and available now on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Android, iOS, Google Play, Epic Games Store, and Steam.

title: Microsoft-Owned GitHub Stuns Followers as It Celebrates AnyPS5 Repo in Now-Deleted Tweet
summary: In a post that’s since been deleted, Microsoft-owned code and software collaboration site GitHub celebrated the AnyPS5 repo “passing 58k stars” from users on the platform as a result of the launch of GTA 6. GitHub even told followers "Happy GTA VImas!" in a tweet that will almost certainly have infurated Rockstar Games, parent company Take-Two, PlayStation, and Xbox.
content: In a post that’s since been deleted, Microsoft-owned code and software collaboration site GitHub celebrated the AnyPS5 repo “passing 58k stars” from users on the platform as a result of the launch of GTA 6. GitHub even told followers "Happy GTA VImas!" in a tweet that will almost certainly have infurated Rockstar Games, parent company Take-Two, PlayStation, and Xbox. “GTA 6 is finally here, sparking one of the biggest weeks in gaming and open source on GitHub,” the post said, before jumping into celebrating the repo. “Does changing where games run cross a legal line?” the tweet asked. This is insane https://t.co/mwU6VIy1nI — MVG (@ModernVintageG) November 26, 2026 There was also an official video attached to the tweet, which highlighted a post from an AnyPS5 coder, via Kotaku . The post in the video said: “We have 3 days until GTA 6 everyone[…]get your agents or deevs[sic] and work.” While the post could easily be the work of a rogue social media person, the optics aren’t good at all. GTA 6 is only officially available on PS5 and Xbox Series X and S, so both Sony and Microsoft have benefited greatly from the game's record-breaking launch. To see a the Microsoft-owned GitHub post a message to its followers essentially encouraging potential piracy is remarkable. IGN has asked for comment, but GitHub obviously realized its mistake — it deleted the tweet, after all — but how it even got approved in the first place is a mystery until the company comments. Take-Two is currently working to take down various homebrew community efforts from GitHub, as the race to release an unofficial GTA 6 PC port heats up. This follows Cyberleek's alleged released of the executable file for the incomplete GTA 6 Xbox build they reportedly leaked the week prior. There’s even a website tracking the various attempts to recompile, emulate, or port the leaked Xbox Series build to PC. The big question for Take-Two is, can it do anything meaningful to stop a working, playable build of GTA 6 on PC from getting into people's hands? GitHub takedowns can only go so far, as the homebrew scenes uses AI to speed along development. Take-Two stands to make billions of dollars more from the official PC release of GTA 6, so any unofficial version is a significant business risk. In a recent interview with IGN sister site RPS , former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij said that Rockstar Games may be keen to port GTA 6 to PC as soon as possible , due to the explosion of AI-generated clones and ports. It's also worth noting that there is extra interest in a PC version of GTA 6 because the console versions target 30fps. The PC version, resumably, will run at 60fps or whatever frame rate your rig is capable of . Earlier this month, Strauss Zelnick, the boss of Take-Two, responded to the threat of AI-assisted reverse-engineering and decompilation of games in an interview with IGN. He said he was taking the issue seriously, and insisted that fans will prefer to play GTA 6 officially, with all its bells and whistles as Rockstar intended, over an unofficial PC version. Here’s the exchange: IGN: We've seen hackers using AI to clone games much faster than ever before, even try to jailbreak consoles. And there is some concern about this leading to potentially GTA 6 being made available on PC unofficially or places that you aren't releasing it. I was just wondering how much of a threat this is to your business? And, is there anything meaningful you can do about it? Strauss Zelnick: I don't think it’s a financial matter, in terms of a threat to our business. I do think it’s a creative matter. It's important to everyone, our developers and our consumers alike, to deliver the experience Rockstar envisions. And at the same time, of course, we protect our intellectual property vigilantly. So we are focused on these concerns. We're not in the least cavalier about them. Technology is advancing quickly. And at the same time, I do think that pretty much everyone wants the Rockstar experience as Rockstar intended. IGN: Related, last week Anthropic confirmed they took steps to block Claude from reverse engineering video games. I would assume you would welcome that. And would you like to see other AI companies like OpenAI do the same thing to prevent people from using these powerful AI models to clone your games? Strauss Zelnick: I think all companies should be protecting intellectual property, their own and everyone else's. And if you're in the intellectual property business, which Anthropic is and OpenAI is, then it seems ironic on the one hand to stomp on someone else's IP and hope that yours is protected. During an investor-focused Q&A following the release of Take-Two’s latest financial report, attended by IGN, Zelnick was asked multiple times about the AI reverse-engineering problem. He, again, had strong words in response, suggesting Take-Two was ready to lawyer up. “This business has been largely immune to piracy concerns forever because of file sizes, complexity of piracy, being connected to servers and the like,” he began. “And undoubtedly, it would be very difficult to replicate the experience of consuming our game as intended because of technical limitations. “That said, it's going to become more of a challenge, as you said, and we're aware of that. So we are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And at the same time, without in any way being cavalier, every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy. So this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it.” Zelnick’s talk about legal activities sparks an obvious question: what can game companies do about AI-assisted reverse engineering? It's a question IGN recently asked when people started to work on a PC port of Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake . title: GTA 6's Chapter 3 Heist Might Be Rockstar's Best Ever Mission, But Only If You Do It Badly
summary: GTA 6's chapter three heist might be Rockstar's best ever mission, but only if you do it badly.
content: Warning: This article contains spoilers for chapter three of GTA 6. Chapter 3 of GTA 6 ends with a bang. It’s arguably Rockstar’s greatest ever mission and a culmination of every bank job the developer has designed since GTA 4’s Three Leaf Clover burst onto the scene. A daring raid on the Sinfrontera National Bank in downtown Vice City, what starts out as a slick operation quickly goes haywire, resulting in shootouts with armored police, helicopters chasing a bus that has had the roof ripped off, and the death of one of your gang members. The funny thing is, you may be reading that and thinking that’s not what happened to you at all. That’s because the back half of The Cartel Heist can go in wildly different directions. You can do it much more cleanly, but it’s nowhere near as fun. Sorry, Nicole. A lot has to go in your favour to execute the perfect heist. Making sure you correctly prep is key, meaning you’ll have to extract all of the info possible out of Monty when he’s dangling over reptilian teeth, protect Pete’s shipment of weapons correctly, and plant enough explosives on the cell towers. Then there’s also everything you have to get going your way inside the mission itself, which is mainly tied to not wasting time and nailing the vault minigame. You can get the full details on everything you’ll need to do, step-by-step, on our excellent guides page . Nail it, and your getaway driver will turn up as planned by the underground entrance; you’ll load up the truck with stacks of cash and simply drive off undetected. There are obvious benefits to doing this. Not only is there the satisfaction of pulling off such a complex job cleanly, but you’ll earn $150,000 from it, rather than the $100,000 you’d otherwise get, plus Nicole, your charming safecracking tutor, will survive. What you will miss out on, though, is one of Rockstar’s finest blockbuster sequences. It makes Three Leaf Clover firmly look like the first draft that it was back in 2008. The path truly branches once you leave the bank’s vault, but in all truth, your fate has likely been long sealed by that point. You’ll have needed to keep a keen eye on your time in the bottom right corner and have made sure all ten bundles of bills have been secured by the time the alarm goes off and all hell breaks loose. That’s when things kick up a notch, and legions of Vice City police and NOOSE enforcers turn up at the front doors. A lobby shootout commences, with enemies turning up from all directions in an effort to stop you from leaving with your haul. It's a fantastic encounter that borders on sensory overload thanks to the rattle of gunfire, thick smoke, and blaring alarms. The slick transitions between characters only add to the sense of cinema, with Lucia throwing a smoke grenade launcher up to the balcony for Jason to catch, punctuated by a highly satisfying second or two of slow motion. This elegantly moves the action onto the streets, allowing you to get a glimpse of the full challenge awaiting you and your gang outside. Michael Mann’s Heat has long been an influence on Grand Theft Auto, but never has the sensation of watching the movie’s signature heist been replicated as well as it has here. It makes Three Leaf Clover firmly look like the first draft that it was back in 2008. As the fight moves outdoors, Raul’s backup plan comes to fruition with Karim arriving behind the wheel of a public bus. Up to this point in GTA 6’s story, the heist leader has remained a mysterious presence, slinking in and out of scenes with an undeniable air of cool. It’s not until now, though, that we get to see him in full flow, leading with calm authority. He’s quickly become one of my favourite characters across the whole Grand Theft Auto series — embodying the swagger and ruthless execution of a lusciously long-maned Danny Ocean. Of course, it would all be too simple for everyone to walk onto the bus and drive off into the sunset. Lucia, Raul, Andrea, and Karim all make it on board, but have to make the tough decision to leave without Jason and Nicole. Having to find an alternative escape route, it calls on Jason to flex all of his military muscles and escort Nicole to safety. Bleeding out thanks to a gunshot to the stomach, she makes it to a SWAT van that Jason takes the wheel of. The chase is on. GTA 6’s big-scale missions are when the dynamic player-switching really comes into its own. Before we know it, we’re back on the bus and having to hold off cars, trucks, and helicopters as Lucia from the back seat. Nothing can prevent the roof from being torn off by some hooks from a nearby truck, though, in what might be the whole mission’s most jaw-dropping moment. It’s just pure flexing from Rockstar at this point, and I’m all for it. Not only does it add to the spectacle, but it makes you rethink how to take down your pursuers due to your cover being violently rearranged. All of that prep work you did on previous missions may not have led to you getting the perfect heist escape, but it still has its benefits here. Manage to protect all of the weapons cargo provided by Pete? You’ll get a very fun grenade launcher to wield here and blow away the opposition with. The number of variables within this mission is staggering, and a real showcase of how the little choices you make as Jason and Lucia affect their story. The whole of chapter three has been building up to this moment, and knowing that every step before it actually meant something makes it all the more rewarding. One final character switch is then made, with Jason tasked with catching up with the bus and getting both him and Nicole on board. Sadly, no matter what you do, once everyone has regrouped, Nicole will die. The sound of the alarm going off in that bank may as well have been the Grim Reaper tolling his bell. It almost feels like this is the canonical way things should go, though. Jason and Lucia’s tale is one of escape, with tragedy, twists, and treachery meeting them at each turn. The Cartel Heist is no different when played this way. It’s pure action thriller filmmaking. Heat, Thief, Ocean's Eleven, The Town, Speed. It has the lot. It has all the gameplay ingredients needed to be considered Rockstar’s greatest ever heist, and perhaps mission full stop. Not only is this mission fantastic from a storytelling perspective, but it’s also a feast of level design. Yes, it may largely take place on rails, but there’s enough wiggle room there for you to change tracks and give the impression of player agency, even when there seems to be little of it on the surface. Under the hood, the gears are always ticking, some of which have been greased hours previously, primed and ready to slot into place. There’s never a dull moment, whether that be in a tense first half soundtracked by the ticking of the clock, or in its balls-to-the-wall explosive second section. Gunfights, safe-cracking, car chases — it has all the gameplay ingredients needed to be considered Rockstar’s greatest ever heist, and perhaps mission full stop. I just find it fascinating that if you happened to do it perfectly, you might not see what the fuss is all about.

title: Lucia Actress Manni L. Perez Issues First Statement Since GTA 6 Launch
summary: Manni L. Perez, the actress who plays Lucia in GTA 6, has issued her first statement since the game came out.
content: Manni L. Perez, the actress who plays Lucia in GTA 6 , has issued her first statement since the game came out. Perez’s role as Lucia Caminos was confirmed when she was nominated in the Best Performance category for this year’s The Game Awards , a day before GTA 6 launched on November 19. She’s now considered the favorite following the game’s critically acclaimed, record-breaking launch. Now, a week later, Perez took to social media to thank fans for the reception to GTA 6. “Life has been such a whirlwind these past couple of days and I just want to take a moment to say thank you,” an Instagram Stories post began. “Thank you to all the new followers, to all the beautiful messages, and the positive reception the game and my character have received. “I've dedicated almost a decade bringing Lucia to life. She's been such a significant part of mine and I am beyond grateful she now gets to be a small part of yours.” “Happy Holiday's y'all.” Perez is an actress with a smattering of credits to her acting resume, including TV guest roles in Jessica Jones, Chicago P.D., and Law & Order: Special Victims Unit. While she hasn't been up to much else over the past few years, it's easy to know why — GTA 6 sounds like it was a pretty involved project. Indeed, Lucia isn’t Perez's first GTA role. In GTA 5, she plays the background character of "Clubber #2," while in GTA Online she voices a blackjack dealer. Meanwhile, Jason actor Dylan Rourke also posted a message of gratitude on Instagram Stories, saying: “Thankful for this wild ride. Gratitude won’t cut it. Make today about the ones you love.” Manni L. Perez shouldn't be confused with Manny Perez, who plays Raul Bautista in GTA 6. This week, Manny Perez bought a PS5 just so he could play the game, saying in a video posted to social media: “Guy, I’m playing and this s**t is crazy! Look how real that looks. I’m learning, I’m loving this, it’s crazy.” Other GTA 6 actors who've started to talk about their work on the game include Lexie Shoaibi, who recently spoke out about her "bittersweet" newfound fame after her character, Mandy, went viral online, and Cocoteo FM radio host Issa Lopez, who described the wild non-disclosure agreement she had to sign before working on the game . title: Another Modder Uses AI to Make a Multiplayer Mode for The Last of Us Part 2 — Will Sony Shut This One Down, Too?
summary: Another modder has used AI to make a multiplayer mode for The Last of Us Part 2, insisting there isn't much Sony can do about it "even if they do shut me down."
content: Another modder has used AI to make a multiplayer mode for The Last of Us Part 2 , insisting there isn't much Sony can do about it "even if they do shut me down." The Last of Us had a brilliant multiplayer mode, with tense gunfights powered by weapon sway, smart cover, and nail-biting in-round crafting that forced you to dig around in your backpack as bullets whizzed over your bonce. That’s why so many people were excited when Naughty Dog announced a Factions multiplayer game in the works based on The Last of Us Part 2 . Naughty Dog, however, eventually realized that making a live-service game would change the studio forever, and cancelled the project to focus instead on its upcoming sci-fi game, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet . The Last of Us Part 2 made some brilliant tweaks to the combat, allowing for better mobility and deeper stealth. The feel of the weapons, the crunch of the impacts, the audiovisual spectacle of it all was just something else, but we can only experience it in single-player, officially. It’s no wonder people want to make Factions happen, even without Sony’s approval. And in September, a promising mod made some big strides towards getting multiplayer working in The Last of Us Part 2. As soon as it started to get traction, however, the mod was sent a cease and desist letter from Sony . “Hey everyone, as you all know, the TLOU 2 Multiplayer mod that has been in development since January was supposed to [be released] this month,” wrote creator 'Speclizer' at the time. “Unfortunately I recently received a letter on behalf of Sony Interactive Entertainment requesting for the mod not to be released. Extremely sad that this never got to see the light of day but I hope you’ll continue to follow me onto the next project, this time something of my own.” Now there’s a new mod hoping to avoid the eye of Sauron, and it’s already out. The mod is called Twelve Weeks and was built specifically for The Last of Us Part 2 Remastered on PC, using, its creator has admitted, generative AI. Modder 'Kellie' admitted to using Claude code for most of the game's development, and AI was even used to write the lore dumps you can find in the game. The art was, however, made using Blender . The Last of Us returns with a new online multiplayer mode called TWELVE WEEKS created for The Last of Us Part 2 Remastered on PC. This free mod is a work in progress allowing players to experience a new version of the beloved Factions multiplayer with tactical survival gameplay https://t.co/2P8Wv4abQb — 𝗩𝗢𝗬𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗥𝗦 𝗥𝗘𝗩𝗘𝗡𝗚𝗘 (@VoyagersRevenge) November 24, 2026 It features reworked levels — Supply Raid and Interrogation for now — with team-based 4v4 combat, new weapons, and character customization. Players can use gadgets like molotovs and smoke bombs, while fighting against other players as the WLF and Seraphites. The mod even adds brutal execution moves. You can grab Twelve Weeks on Nexus Mods . However, the mod probably won't last long. The modders have attempted to cover their backs with a repository disclaimer that said: "Twelve Weeks is an unofficial fan project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Sony Interactive Entertainment or Naughty Dog. The Last of Us is a trademark of its owners. You need your own legitimately purchased copy of the game (Steam). This repository contains no game files and no assets taken from the game." Will Sony take action? In a reply to someone on YouTube , Kellie said the previous Factions mod got hit by Sony because it was paywalled. "Mine is released already for free and in open source," they said. "Since people have the source code to the full mod already, there ain't much they can do even if they do shut me down." While The Last of Us Online was canceled, there are hints that Naughty Dog may be ready to return to the series for The Last of Us 3 . And then there is HBO's The Last of Us TV series , which is currently shooting its third (and likely last) season.

title: GTA 6 Weather Still Not Varied Even After the Patch? PS5 Players Are Sharing a Method That May Help Rain and Thunderstorms Kick In
summary: Rockstar recently dropped the first post-launch patch for GTA 6 which, among other things, included a fix for the game’s lack of weather variety. Some players were left still experiencing issues, but now there’s seemingly a workaround for PS5 players specifically.
content: Rockstar recently dropped the first post-launch patch for GTA 6 which, among other things, included a fix for the game’s lack of weather variety. Some players were left still experiencing issues, but now there’s seemingly a workaround for PS5 players specifically. Lack of weather variety was something I noticed myself during the game’s review period, but Rockstar deployed a small fix during that time too. It was hard to tell whether it was working as intended because the weather also grows more stark as you move through the game. “The weather types change throughout each day, and the overall weather pattern changes per chapter, evolving from generally very good weather in the first chapter to much more changeable and stormy in the last chapter,” said Owen Shepherd, vice president of art: lighting and rendering at Rockstar, when I asked. “This is analogous to Florida’s weather patterns in winter through to summer autumn. During the first chapters there are pockets of rain but due to the localization of weather it is possible to miss these." However, it seems like the issue persisted into the live version of the game, blurring the line between thematically appropriate and accurate weather patterns and unintended bug. The latest patch fixed this for the most part, but some players found they were still experiencing minimal weather changes. If you’re having the same issue, there might be a fix (discovered by X / Twitter user @mauricioce85796 ). On PS5, you need to turn off your console and boot it into safe mode by holding the power button down until it beeps. From there, choose option six and select “clear system cache.” According to people who have tested it, this forces the patch to do its job. “I have 56 hours in this game so far and I haven’t experienced any dramatic weather,” said Rockstar fan account Gameroll . “I did this and upon loading I was IMMEDIATELY met with this storm. I’m delighted.” Of course, this could be a placebo, but players in the replies have been trying it and immediately seeing results. “Guys, I can confirm, it’s working,” said one happy X / Twitter user who showcased a rainy clip. “Can confirm, weather is more varied!” said another . Clearing your cache on PS5 won’t delete game saves or installed games. It just deletes temporary system files and lets the console recreate fresh ones without erasing your games, saved data, screenshots, or account settings. It helps resolve system feature glitches, slow performance, stuttering, app or game launch errors, and network or sync hiccups. People have been doing it for years, claiming to see performance benefits as a result. Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? title: GTA 6 Players Have Found a Cheeky Method to Quickly Steal ATMs
summary: Somewhere around the middle of GTA 6 you unlock the ability to rob ATMs. Any ATM marked green can be pulled out of the wall and cracked open.
content: Warning! Potential spoilers for GTA 6 follow. Somewhere around the middle of GTA 6 you unlock the ability to rob ATMs. Any ATM marked green can be pulled out of the wall and cracked open (check out IGN's guide to all ATM locations in GTA 6 if you need help finding one). First, though, you need to be able to deal with marked bills through a fence called Yasmini, otherwise the money inside the ATM is worthless and a dye pack will explode in your face. When I got to snatching ATMs, I thought it was cool, but the juice didn’t seem worth the squeeze. It’s kinda hard to keep things on the downlow when you’re backing a truck up to an ATM, ripping it out of a wall, and tearing down the street with the thing still attached, hoping it’ll burst open and spill its contents onto the street. And when it finally does break open, you have to shoot the money drawers open to get to the goods inside — all for a payout between $6,000-$10,000. It wasn’t worth the effort, honestly. But there’s a new trick players have discovered to crack those eggs immediately and move onto the next before the cops even know you’re there. I’ve tried it, and like Todd Howard famously once said: it just works. How to quickly steal an ATM in GTA 6 Here’s what you do. First, you need a truck or other heavy vehicle with a winch attachment at the back. You reverse up to the ATM like normal, and the winch connects to the machine. Now drive forward until the line is taut. From there, get out of your vehicle and walk up to the ATM with a C4 charge. Hold down aim, and a prompt to place it on the ATM should show up, allowing you to set it on the front with Circle/B. Or throw it at the front of the machine — whatever works. Once it’s in place, you want to get back in your car and accelerate hard. When it pulls out of the wall, keep dragging it but immediately press unhook, followed by the same button to detonate your charge. It’s important these two actions happen immediately after each other, because the ATM needs to be moving when the explosion happens or the drawers can stay inside the machine. Done correctly, you can walk over and scoop up the cash and escape before the cops even arrive at the scene. They’ll still be figuring out what happened while you’re hooking up to the next machine, pulling, and sparking up a Cuban. If you need more C4, there’s a free stash of the stuff in the back of Yasmani’s. You can also top up at any Ammunation. A Simple Trick for Faster ATM Robberies GTA 6 https://t.co/lo6aWdupew — LUCKY (@Badboy1B) November 25, 2026 Players have been trying to find ways to make quick money in GTA 6 since launch, but most of them are boring exploits. This, though, I can get onboard with because it’s just playing the game as intended in an efficient way, and it’s great fun to slip in and out without the cops getting a whiff of you. title: Rockstar Explains Why it Added Consequences to GTA 6's Violence and Crimes
summary: Rockstar Games boss Rob Nelson has explained why the studio added the divisive criminal profile system to GTA 6.
content: Rockstar Games boss Rob Nelson has explained why the studio added the divisive criminal profile system to GTA 6 . In an interview with Eurogamer , Nelson was asked about Rockstar's approach to the systems and themes in GTA 6. He said that a lot of it was born out of all of the work they put into Red Dead Redemption 2, specifically having a reactive world that responds to the player's behavior and choices. He explained that there was a desire to evolve the GTA experience and to "give players choices to interact with the world beyond just violence, beyond just 'down the barrel of a gun.'" That means players can now point a gun at someone and threaten them, rather than having to beat or kill them to steal their money. The threat of violence is just as prevalent as the violence itself in GTA 6, and it also plays into the morality-adjacent system that is your criminal profile. The game doesn't explicitly punish you for doing bad things, because it's GTA, and you're bound to do bad things. However, it judges you on how harsh you are. If you rob a store with minimal force or only attack people if they draw on you first, attempting to minimize casualties, your profile won't change. If you go in and kill everyone, the level may decrease. This prompted Rockstar to expand NPC interactions even further. If you drew a gun in GTA 5, no one cared until it was actively pointed at them. Now, people will begin to quietly scurry away if they see you pull a rifle out of your trunk. Nelson explained that while the powerful rampages were fun for a while in previous games, they lacked substance and would get old quickly. In GTA 6, the process to start mowing people down takes a bit more thought because you don't have an endless pocket of weapons anymore. "You have to call your car," says Nelson. "You have to pop a car trunk and get [a weapon], and now I'm walking, and now people are noticing, but they're sort of sidling away, and it's more believable. And then they're still fleeing in terror, but then there's people who also have guns, and they're shooting at you, or you try to hold somebody up, and they pull a gun, or they grab it, and then you have to deal with them. "And then, you choose. You're trying to jack somebody off a motorcycle, and they pull a gun on you, and you have to blow their head off, and it's like, 'You shouldn't have made me do that!' And so then it has more meaning, and it's more funny in a way when it's a little bit more pointed. And you can still go on those rampages and basically smash your criminal profile until it breaks, and then you enter this irredeemable state, which basically says, 'I reject your criminal profile system! I don't want it.'" The more realistic approach with GTA 6 has been a bit divisive for purists. Some don't want consequences; they want a power fantasy, and GTA 6 is decidely not that. If you want a supercar, it's going to take you dozens of hours before you can steal one. There's a progression to the chaos. For some, that's more rewarding. For others who want that quick fix, it's cumbersome. It'll be interesting to see how Rockstar looks at all of the responses to the game and how that informs the next GTA. Will they go further down this path or will they try to find a greater middle ground? The game certainly isn't hurting despite some vocal critics. GTA 6 is the highest rated game in history on Metacritic and generated nearly $4 billion in revenue in its first 24 hours , making it the biggest entertainment launch in history. IGN gave the game a 10 out of 10 , praising it for its depth and detail. "Exquisitely detailed, endlessly ripe for experimentation, and uncompromisingly engineered, GTA 6 has not stopped astonishing me since I started it," reads an excerpt from our review. "I regularly find myself in love with video games, but it’s extraordinarily rare that I find myself in complete awe of them. Put simply, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the single most impressive video game I have ever played."

title: Rockstar Games Issues Statement as Union Vote Fails
summary: The Rockstar Games union vote has failed, with 75% voting against a recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union.
content: The Rockstar Games union vote has failed, with 75% voting against a recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union. The shock result comes following the hugely successful launch of GTA 6 , which has set records as the biggest entertainment launch of all time. Workers at Rockstar Games voted 25% in favour of and 75% against a recognition agreement with the IWGB. The terms of the recognition deal were agreed following months of negotiations that took place even as the IWGB and Rockstar clashed over the firing of 31 workers for allegedly leaking company secrets in October last year. The IWGB has alleged the workers were unlawfully fired, and have accused Rockstar Games of union busting. The vote overlapped with the closing submissions of the employment tribunal, which ended earlier this month. Judgement is currently pending. If the IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union had won the vote, it would have become the biggest recognised union in the UK games industry. The ballot saw 93.2% turnout, with 1,544 employees across Rockstar’s UK sites in Edinburgh, Leeds, Lincoln, Dundee, and London participating. 1,163 team members voted against IWGB recognition (75.3%), while 381 voted in favour (24.7%). In a statement issued to IGN, Rockstar Games head of publishing, Jennifer Kolbe, said the company was “extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of GTA 6.” “This result reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong,” Kolbe continued. “As we look ahead, we're excited to build on all we've accomplished together.” The IWGB insisted that Rockstar workers would keep organizing without a formal union recognition deal after the ballot. The IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union shared the following statement: “For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society — this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen. “Whilst we haven’t emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for new kinds of conversation to start happening. People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We heard from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions can lead us. “A recognition agreement would have marked a path towards greater workplace democracy. But it’s one route of many. At Rockstar we have already won, and will continue to win, tangible changes that improve our everyday lives. We’ll keep fighting for a say. For pay transparency, contractual overtime pay, and protections against AI and layoffs. “The power to shape our working lives has always been, and will always be, in our hands.” Kolbe had indicated Rockstar’s willingness to work with staff on union recognition, recently telling Bloomberg : “We go where the team goes. So if they want a union, they will have a union.” Photo by Lesley Martin / AFP via Getty Images.

title: Rockstar North Chief Was Praying GTA 6's Big Story Reveal Stayed Under Wraps Ahead of Launch
summary: Rockstar North has explained why it was so important that GTA 6's big early story reveal stayed under wraps before the game came out.
content: Warning! This article contains spoilers for the prologue of GTA 6 . GTA 6’s prologue hides a surprise that somehow managed to stay a secret all the way up to players finding out for themselves. And Rockstar North, it turns out, was praying for it not to leak ahead of launch. During the game’s opening stretch, the story of how Lucia ends up in a Leonida prison is told. This isn’t the surprising part — ever since GTA 6 Trailer 1 we’ve known she’d end up behind bars at some point — but the person she was at a diner moments before her arrest is. Tomás, a few-month-old baby and son of Lucia and Jason, is left behind by his mother in GTA 6’s first truly shocking reveal. Given the history of leaks associated with GTA 6 , it feels like a minor miracle that Tommy’s existence remained a complete unknown until launch. This was something that Rob Nelson, co-studio head at Rockstar North, was keenly aware of. “No, we never were going to [reveal it]," he told VGC in an interview that took place just before GTA 6 came out last week. "I am still holding on. Fingers crossed, how many more days? I’m praying it stays under wraps. Given everything that we’ve gone through, every day I’m just like, ‘Please, please don’t do that, please don’t do that.'” As we’ve written about at IGN, the existence of Tomás in GTA 6 is the key to its whole design . It’s what powers Jason and Lucia’s tale, and encourages the player to strive to make more and more money as those family savings goals get higher and higher. It connects us to the characters, and creates a shared objective between us and them. We aren’t simply committing crime for crime’s sake, but doing so with the prospect of being reunited with their son at the end of it. You can see why such a powerful and surprising narrative device would want to have been kept under wraps by Rockstar. It’s the first, and by no means the only, shocking revelation of GTA 6, all the more effective when witnessed firsthand. “We never were going to [reveal it],” Nelson explained. “It’s meant to shock. We were watching everyone speculate about the nature of their relationship and Jason’s character, and that takes it in a completely different context. You have something to strive for beyond a huge bank account at the end.” We’ve got the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide here on IGN, complete with comprehensive walkthroughs up to Chapter 4 , guides for the Optional Missions and Illegal Operations you’ll find in Leonida, and much more. title: Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 Patch 16.0 Goes Live, Expands Vanguard Class, Makes Big Balance Changes, and Much More
summary: Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 still receives significant support two years after launch. We’re now up to patch 16, which makes significant balance changes to the game. Check out the patch notes.
content: Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 still receives significant support two years after launch. We’re now up to patch 16.0, which makes significant balance changes to the game. In terms of new features, we’ve got a major expansion of the Vanguard class’ combat abilities (the Grapnel Launcher can now be used at close range!), the new Revenge status effect (hitting enemies afflicted with Revenge also deals damage to nearby enemies), and Wargear 2.3 (Bulwark can now equip and customize Cloak!). As for cosmetics, the hotly anticipated Deathwatch Champion Pack is out now as part of the Season Pass. There’s also a Mortifactors Cosmetic Pack. I’ve put the balance changes as part of the patch notes below, if you want to skip to them to see what’s happened to your class. Also interesting is the note about tech improvements with patch 16. Publisher Focus Entertainment says loading times have improved, which players will welcome. There are also memory optimizations, “minor” performance improvements, and “general” connectivity improvements. Anyone who’s played or is still playing Space Marine 2 will hope these improvements are meaningful. Focus has said that next year, Space Marine 2 will receive three more updates until its third anniversary. Patch 17, 18 and 19 will offer free content as well as Season Pass 3 content with the cosmetic DLCs. There’s a lot of excitement around Patch 17, which adds a brand-new class, the Apothecary , complete with its signature Absolvor Bolt Pistol. Patch 17 also adds a new Operation and fresh Heroic weapons, and a rework of the Heavy class. A new Imperial Fist Champion Pack and a Cosmetic Pack for the Minotaurs chapter are also on the way. The Switch 2 version of Space Marine 2, however, is delayed out of 2026 into 2027. “Considering its current polishing needs, we are constrained to pushing the release to 2027,” Focus said. title: Watching TV in GTA 6 Is More Depressing Than Fun, Except for One Show
summary: GTA 6's TV content is impressive on a technical level, but apart from one standout show, it's not all that fun to actually watch.
content: It seems there’s almost nothing you can’t do in Grand Theft Auto VI, other than solicit prostitutes . Far more than just being a murder and crime spree simulator, the game allows you to kick back and do everything from play basketball to remodel your house to work out at the gym. And yes, that long list of side activities includes watching television. GTA 6 includes multiple channels of original programming , featuring everything from breaking Vice City news reports to Adult Swim-style animated sitcoms to cheesy telenovelas. As with so much about the new game, the level of detail Rockstar undertook here is impressive. But despite all that, I found that actually sitting down to watch TV in-game wasn’t quite the entertaining experience I was hoping for. If anything, it was a little depressing. Weazel News: Satire or Sad Reality? To recap, there are three live TV channels in GTA 6 - the Fox News-spoofing Weazel News, the Telemundo parody Megamundo, and the travel-focused Visit Leonida. For the purposes of this piece, I’m mostly focusing on the former channel. Megamundo is a fun sendup of traditional Spanish-language soap operas, but not having any real attachment to that genre, it’s a joke that only has so much mileage for me. And Visit Leonida is definitely the most limited of the three channels. With Weazel News, you have a smorgasbord of faux-TV content, all of which focuses on lampooning the right-wing news sector, reality TV, and general American culture. This stream cycles through various breaking news reports, a mockumentary-style series called “The Tyrone Show,” and several different animated sitcoms. And commercials. Dozens and dozens of satirical commercials for all sorts of in-universe products and services. Initially, you can’t help but sit back and admire the sheer effort that went into making all this content. The TV channels are a very minor feature in the game, and I’m sure many people won’t even really pay attention to them amid all the other countless side activities. The simple fact that you can spend literal hours just sitting in front of a fake TV and not really see any repeat content is impressive. But once the initial novelty wears off, watching TV isn’t what I’d describe as one of the more rewarding pastimes in GTA 6. Weazel News actually left me feeling a bit stressed out and unhappy after a while. It was hard to put my finger on it at first, but I think what it comes down to is that the political and social satire hits a little too close to home. For a Scottish-based studio, Rockstar North is generally pretty adept at satirizing American culture with these games - whether it’s remixing the best elements of classic crime films or lampooning the average American’s love of fast food, beer, and guns. You get a heaping helping of all of that with Weazel TV, particularly in the many faux-commercials where colorful characters hawk various brands of alcohol or campaign for a missile launcher in every home or what have you. The problem is that this material no longer feels as outlandish as it once might have. The sad truth is that real life in the US moved beyond parody at some point in the last 10-15 years. It’s something that a lot of sources of satire have dealt with lately, from South Park to The Onion. How do you top reality when reality has become so unhinged and unbelievable? GTA’s TV content is in the same boat. A lot of it doesn’t feel particularly far removed from reality anymore. There really are people unironically spouting the same kind of jingoistic nonsense you see in these fake commercials. Between extreme right-wing news channels and the digital hellscape that is social media, there’s a real cultural brain rot that’s taken hold. Watching Weazel TV is more an uncomfortable reminder of where we are as a society than a truly unbelievable parody. That’s part of it, anyway. The other issue is that some of the Weazel TV humor feels a bit unnecessarily mean-spirited, particularly anything involving the news broadcasts and Tyrone’s sexually charged misadventures. Rockstar really goes all-in on the “Florida Man” humor, mirroring the sorts of kooky regional headlines and weird characters we’ve all read about online. Through the fictionalized state of Leonida, it paints the real Florida as this unending wasteland of deranged hillbillies and unrepentant criminals. And, yes, Florida has more than its fair share of odd residents, but many perfectly lovely people live there also. Some of the Weazel TV humor feels a bit unnecessarily mean-spirited, particularly anything involving the news broadcasts and Tyrone’s sexually charged misadventures. I always look to King of the Hill as the gold standard when it comes to satirizing a specific American subculture. That animated sitcom is a clear parody of small-town Texan life, but it never settles for leaning on stereotypes or punching down on its colorful cast of characters. They’re all surprisingly nuanced and fully realized for what might seem at first like a bunch of goofy, beer-chugging rednecks. GTA’s main cast of characters may get a similarly nuanced treatment, by and large, but the same can’t really be said for the goofballs who appear on Weazel News. Unlike King of the Hill, this TV content does gleefully punch down, and that means it doesn’t fully sit right. The Joy of Rockstar’s Right Wing That all being said, there is one good reason to keep Jason’s butt planted on the couch and stay tuned to Weazel News. The channel’s animated sitcoms generally do a better job than the other shows when it comes to providing an amusing dose of escapism. It’s easy to picture any one of these shows having a run on Adult Swim in between reruns of Rick and Morty, whether it’s the stoner humor-focused Macca & Friends or the aggressively copaganda-minded “children’s program” Barnyard Blue. But the real success story in this area is definitely Right Wing. Right Wing is basically a superhero cartoon about a dimwitted defender of Truth, Justice, and the American Way, or the stereotypical ultraconservative vision of it, anyway. Each episode pits the hero and his handler (a very George W. Bush-coded President) against a different conservative boogeyman villain like the border wall-busting Immigrantasma or the psychically-empowered Educated Woman. Ultimately, Right Wing usually doesn’t save the day so much as he makes a giant ass of himself and exposes the hypocrisy of the anti-left, anti-feminist, anti-LGBTQ+ agenda. All in a day’s work. Of all the hours of TV content programmed into GTA 6, the Right Wing cartoons are easily my favorite. They’re both hilarious and insightful. The satire works in a way the more direct gags in the rest of the Weazel News content don’t always land. Again, this legitimately feels like something that could run on Adult Swim and find a sizable following in the process. Only time will tell what sort of additional content Rockstar will add to GTA 6 in the months and years to come. I’m sure the studio is currently heads-down on getting the next version of GTA Online ready for what’s sure to be a historic launch. But I sincerely hope the developer looks at expanding the currently available TV content. There are lessons to be learned in terms of what works and doesn’t work on Weazel News. The main lesson: focus less on trying to satirize the unsatirizable aspects of American culture and focus more on these wonderful little adult cartoons. Season 2 of Right Wing would be much appreciated. For mroe GTA fun, check out IGN's Grand Theft Auto VI review and find out why Jason buying Lucia flowers is the game's dumbest controversy .
